# rustnum

> rustnum is a NumPy-style n-dimensional array library for pure Rust. One type, `Array<T>`, covers 0-d, 1-d and n-d data. Function names, argument order and panic messages follow NumPy. Write `use rustnum as np;` and call `np::zeros`, `np::linalg::solve`, `np::random::Rng`. Element types: f32 f64 i32 i64 u8 usize bool. Views are copy-on-write, not write-through. Misuse (bad shape, index, axis) panics with NumPy's message; bad data (files, singular matrix) returns `np::Result`. Full NumPy table: docs/NUMPY_MAPPING.md. Contract: docs/API.md.

## Rules for writing rustnum code
- Always `use rustnum as np;`. `shape` is `&[usize]`, `axis` is `isize` (negative allowed).
- No keyword arguments. `a.sum(axis=1)` becomes `a.sum_axis(1)`. No keepdims: use `.expand_dims(axis)`.
- Float literals need `.0`: `np::arange(0.0, 5.0, 1.0)`. `np::array![1, 2]` is `Array<i32>`.
- Borrow to keep arrays: `&a + &b`. `a + b` moves both.
- Scalars work on either side: `&a * 2.0`, `1.0 - &a`. The scalar type must equal the element type.
- Math is a method: `a.exp()`, not `np::exp(&a)`. Exceptions: maximum, minimum, power, arctan2, hypot, where_.
- `where` is `where_`. `-1` in reshape needs `reshape_infer(&[-1, 3])`.
- Comparisons are methods returning `Array<bool>`: `a.gt(0.5)`, `a.eq_elem(&b)`. `a == b` returns one bool.
- Fallible calls need `?`: `np::linalg::solve`, `inv`, `cholesky`, `lstsq`, all `np::io` functions.
- Random methods need `let mut rng = np::random::Rng::seed(42);`. Streams differ from NumPy.
- A slice is a view, but a write never changes the parent. Use `a.slice_assign(..)` to write into part of an array.

## 10 NumPy to rustnum translations
```
np.arange(0, 6).reshape(2, 3)        np::arange(0.0, 6.0, 1.0).reshape(&[2, 3])
np.zeros((2, 3))                     np::zeros::<f64>(&[2, 3])
a + b                                &a + &b
a[:, 1]                              a.slice(&np::s![.., 1])
a[::2, 1:]                           a.slice(&np::s![..;2, 1..])
a.sum(axis=0)                        a.sum_axis(0)
a @ b                                a.matmul(&b)
np.linalg.solve(A, y)                np::linalg::solve(&a, &y)?
np.where(a > 0, a, 0.0)              np::where_(&a.gt(0.0), &a, 0.0)
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)      let mut rng = np::random::Rng::seed(42);
```

## Types and traits
- `Array<T>` — the array. Cheap to clone (shared buffer). Implements Clone Debug Display PartialEq Default Send Sync.
- `Element` — all element types. `Num: Element` — f32 f64 i32 i64 u8 usize. `Float: Num` — f32 f64.
- `IntoArray<T>` — anything array-like: `T`, `Array<T>`, `&Array<T>`, `Vec<T>`, `&[T]`, `[T; N]`.
- `np::Error` — variants include Singular, NotPositiveDefinite, Shape(String), DType. `np::Result<T>`.

## Construction
- `np::array![1.0, 2.0]`, `np::array![[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]]` — array literal (ragged panics)
- `Array::from_vec(data, &[2, 3])` — from Vec and shape
- `Array::from_shape_fn(&[2, 3], |idx| value)` — np.fromfunction
- `Array::scalar(v)` — 0-d array
- `Array::from(vec)`, `iter.collect::<Array<T>>()` — 1-d
- `np::zeros::<T>(shape)`, `np::ones::<T>(shape)` — filled arrays
- `np::full(shape, v)` — constant
- `np::zeros_like(&a)`, `np::ones_like(&a)`, `np::full_like(&a, v)`
- `np::arange(start, stop, step)` — all three required, same type
- `np::linspace(start, stop, num)` — floats, endpoint included
- `np::logspace(start, stop, num)` — base 10
- `np::eye::<T>(n)`, `np::identity::<T>(n)`
- `np::diag(&v)` — 1-d to matrix, matrix to 1-d
- `np::tri::<T>(n)`, `np::tril(&a)`, `np::triu(&a)`
- `np::meshgrid(&x, &y)` — (X, Y), indexing xy

## Attributes and access
- `a.shape()` — &[usize]
- `a.ndim()`, `a.size()`, `a.len()` (axis 0, panics on 0-d), `a.is_empty()`
- `a.strides()` — in elements. `a.dtype()` — "float64" etc.
- `a.is_contiguous()`
- `a[[i, j]]`, `a[[i, j]] = v` — index with an array of usize
- `a.get(&[i, j])` — value. `a.set(&[i, j], v)`
- `a.item()` — the only value (size must be 1)
- `a.to_vec()` — Vec<T> in C order. `a.as_slice()` — Option<&[T]>, Some if contiguous
- `a.iter()` — elements in C order. `for x in &a` also works
- `a.to_contiguous()`, `a.copy()` (deep copy)
- `a.astype::<U>()` — cast, truncates like NumPy
- `a.map(|x| ..)` — new array. `a.mapv_inplace(|x| ..)`. `a.zip_map(&b, |x, y| ..)` — broadcasts
- `a.fill(v)`

## Indexing and slicing
- `np::s![1..3, .., -1]` — slice spec. Forms: `a..b` `a..` `..b` `..` `a..=b`, one index drops the axis, `;step`
- `a.slice(&np::s![..;2, 1..;-1])` — O(1) view
- `a.slice_assign(&np::s![0, ..], v)` — write into a region, v is array-like and broadcasts
- `a.index_axis(axis, i)`, `a.row(i)`, `a.col(j)` — drop an axis (row, col are 2-d only)
- `a.mask(&m)` — a[m], 1-d result, m: Array<bool> with a's shape
- `a.mask_assign(&m, v)` — a[m] = v
- `a.take(&[0, 2], axis)` — np.take with usize indices
- `np::nonzero(&a)` — Vec<Array<usize>>. `np::argwhere(&a)`
- `np::searchsorted(&sorted, v)` — usize

## Operators
- `+ - * / %` — all borrow combinations, plus scalar on either side. Broadcast.
- `-a` — signed and float types. `+= -= *= /= %=` — right side Array, &Array or scalar
- `a.eq_elem(b)`, `a.ne_elem(b)`, `a.lt(b)`, `a.le(b)`, `a.gt(b)`, `a.ge(b)` — Array<bool>, b array-like
- `& | ^ !` on `Array<bool>`. `np::logical_and(&m1, &m2)`, `logical_or`, `logical_xor`, `logical_not(&m)`
- `a.allclose(&b, rtol, atol)` — bool, floats. `np::isclose(&a, &b, rtol, atol)` — Array<bool>
- `a.array_equal(&b)`
- `a.broadcast_to(&[3, 4])` — view. `np::broadcast_arrays(&a, &b)`. `np::broadcast_shapes(&s1, &s2)` — Option<Vec<usize>>

## Element-wise math (methods on float arrays, return new array)
- `exp exp2 expm1 log log2 log10 log1p sqrt cbrt square reciprocal` — log is natural log
- `sin cos tan arcsin arccos arctan sinh cosh tanh`
- `floor ceil round trunc abs sign` — abs, sign, square, clip also work on integers
- `a.powf(p)` — float exponent. `a.powi(n)` — integer exponent
- `a.clip(lo, hi)` — method only
- `a.is_nan()`, `a.is_inf()`, `a.is_finite()` — Array<bool>
- `a.sigmoid()`, `a.relu()` — extras, not NumPy
- `np::maximum(&a, &b)`, `np::minimum(&a, &b)` — broadcast, NaN propagates. Scalars allowed.
- `np::power(&a, &b)`, `np::arctan2(&y, &x)`, `np::hypot(&a, &b)`
- `np::where_(&cond, x, y)` — np.where(cond, x, y), x and y array-like

## Reductions (whole array returns a value; `_axis(axis)` removes that axis)
- `sum prod min max` — T. `sum_axis prod_axis min_axis max_axis`
- `mean var std` — floats only. `mean_axis var_axis std_axis`
- `var_ddof(ddof)`, `std_ddof(ddof)` — whole array only
- `argmin argmax` — usize, flat index. `argmin_axis argmax_axis` — Array<usize>
- `any all` — bool. `any_axis all_axis`
- `cumsum cumprod` — flat 1-d. `cumsum_axis cumprod_axis` — keep shape
- `count_nonzero ptp` — whole array
- `median`, `median_axis(axis)`, `percentile(q)` — floats, q in 0..=100
- `nansum nanmean nanmax nanmin` — floats, whole array
- Empty min/max/argmin/argmax panic.
- Keep dims: `a.sum_axis(1).expand_dims(1)`

## Shape manipulation
- `a.reshape(&[2, 3])` — usize. `a.reshape_infer(&[-1, 3])` — isize, one -1 allowed
- `a.ravel()`, `a.flatten()`
- `a.t()` — reverse axes (view). `a.transpose(&[1, 0, 2])`, `permute_axes` (same)
- `a.swapaxes(a0, a1)`, `a.moveaxis(src, dst)`
- `a.squeeze()`, `a.squeeze_axis(axis)`, `a.expand_dims(axis)`
- `a.flip(axis)`, `a.flip_all()`, `a.roll(shift, axis)`
- `a.repeat(n, axis)`, `a.tile(&[2, 3])`
- `a.sort()` (last axis, NaN last), `a.sort_axis(axis)`, `a.argsort()`, `a.argsort_axis(axis)` — argsort gives Array<usize>
- `np::concatenate(&[&a, &b], axis)`, `np::stack(&[&a, &b], axis)`, `np::vstack(&[&a, &b])`, `np::hstack(&[&a, &b])`
- `np::split(&a, sections, axis)`, `np::array_split(&a, sections, axis)` — Vec<Array<T>>
- `np::unique(&a)` — sorted 1-d. `np::unique_counts(&a)` — (values, counts)
- `np::pad(&a, width, value)` — constant padding

## Linear algebra
- `a.matmul(&b)` — 1-d, 2-d, batched n-d. f32/f64 use matrixmultiply.
- `a.dot(&b)`, `a.trace()`
- `np::linalg::outer(&a, &b)`, `inner(&a, &b)`
- `np::linalg::det(&a)` — F
- `np::linalg::inv(&a)?`, `solve(&a, &b)?`, `lstsq(&a, &b)?` — Result<Array<F>>. Error::Singular if singular
- `np::linalg::pinv(&a)`
- `np::linalg::norm(&a)` — F. `norm_axis(&a, ord, axis)`
- `np::linalg::cholesky(&a)?` — lower triangle. Error::NotPositiveDefinite
- `np::linalg::qr(&a)` — (q, r), reduced
- `np::linalg::eigh(&a)` — (values ascending, vectors as columns), symmetric input
- `np::linalg::svd(&a)` — (u, s descending, vt), reduced
- `np::linalg::matrix_rank(&a)` — usize. `matrix_power(&a, n)`

## Random
- `let mut rng = np::random::Rng::seed(42);` or `Rng::from_entropy()`
- `rng.random(shape)` — [0, 1). `rng.uniform(lo, hi, shape)`
- `rng.normal(mean, std, shape)`, `rng.standard_normal(shape)`
- `rng.integers(lo, hi, shape)` — Array<i64>, hi exclusive
- `rng.choice(&a, n, replace)`, `rng.shuffle(&mut a)`, `rng.permutation(n)`
- `rng.binomial(n, p, shape)`, `rng.poisson(lam, shape)`, `rng.exponential(scale, shape)`
- Same seed gives same numbers on every platform. Not NumPy's numbers.

## I/O
- `np::io::save_npy(path, &a)?`, `np::io::load_npy::<T>(path)?` — NumPy .npy v1/v2. Wrong dtype gives Error::DType
- `np::io::save_csv(path, &a, ',')?`, `np::io::load_csv::<T>(path, ',', skip_header)?`
- `np::io::to_npy_bytes(&a)`, `np::io::from_npy_bytes::<T>(&bytes)?`

## Printing
- `println!("{a}")` — NumPy layout: `[[1. 2.]\n [3. 4.]]`, bools `[ True False]`, 0-d as the bare value
- `println!("{a:?}")` — `array([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]], dtype=float64)`

## Not supported in v0.1
complex numbers, float16, datetime/struct dtypes, masked arrays, fft, polynomial, .npz, einsum, fancy indexing on several axes, np.cov, np.diff, linalg.eig.

## Files
- README.md — overview and quick start
- docs/NUMPY_MAPPING.md — every NumPy call with its rustnum equivalent
- docs/API.md — binding API contract
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md — internals and how to add a function
- rustnum/examples/ — quickstart, linear_regression, pca, kmeans, image_ops
